title: Runtime warmup and regression illumination suite
creator: Diego Alvarez
description: Create a focused pre-deploy suite that primes runtime state (KV caches, tokenizer caches, model variants) and generates a compact, explainable regression signal we call 'illumination' for quick attribution. The goal is to detect subtle throughput and tail-latency regressions caused by kernel selection, quantization changes, or sequence-length distribution shifts before any rollout to LTS or Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: A compact 'warmup profile' can be produced for a given model+config in under 10 minutes
Detection pipeline flags >5% p95 latency regression or >8% throughput loss compared to baseline and emits an attribution hint (kernel/sequence/kv) in CI logs
Warmup run produces a small artifact (JSON) with token distribution, KV hit-rate, and representative per-seq-length latency buckets
Artifacts are stored in the releases bucket and linked from the release notes for auditability
Procedure documented and runnable by on-call within 15 minutes with playbook steps
implementation_plan: Design lightweight warmup harness that replays representative prompt bundles sampled from production-telemetry; include a deterministic subset for rebuilds
Instrument runtime to emit KV priming metrics (primed_keys, kv_hit_ratio_by_prefix_length) and per-kernel counters
Build an 'illumination' aggregator that correlates perf deltas with kernel selection, quantization path, and sequence-length skew
Create CI job that runs warmup+illumination on PRs touching runtime heuristics or kernel selection tables
Expose a console panel (read-only) that shows latest warmup artifact and delta hints for each release candidate
test_plan: Unit tests for the warmup harness input validation and sampling logic
End-to-end smoke job in a small cluster that verifies KV priming increases hit_rate baseline by >10% for known workloads
Regression detection tests that simulate kernel-induced slowdowns to validate illumination attribution
Backfill historical runs for three prior releases to sanity-check false-positive rate
Runbook-driven manual verification by Eng-Oncall and Release Manager before promoting to LTS channel
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Kickoff with runtime, infra, and observability. Agreed on minimal artifact schema for 'warmup profile' (token_hist, kv_hits, per_seq_latency).
2026-03-08: Prototype harness that replays a 2k prompt bundle; initial runs show KV hit_ratio variance across quantized kernels (investigating sampling bias).
2026-03-10: Added lightweight attribution heuristics that compare per-seq-length deltas and mark likely cause (e.g., 'kernel selection shift' or 'seq-propateriation').
2026-03-12: CI job draft created (ci/warmup-illumination.yml). Failing PRs will block runtime kernel table merges if p95 regression > 7%. Need policy approval from Release Manager.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Warmup workload may not represent edge customer sequences -> Mitigation: maintain a deterministic sample + periodic re-sampling from telemetry and label source-of-sample
Risk: False attribution due to noisy measurements -> Mitigation: require 3 repeated runs and compare per-kernel counters before signaling
Risk: CI time increase -> Mitigation: make job optional for low-priority PRs and run full illumination only on release candidate pipelines
Risk: Sensitive telemetry in sample -> Mitigation: apply PII-freeing transforms and use only tokenized hashes in artifacts
